## Finding

At pinned `origin/main` `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, `src/compiler2/world.rs:2288-2291` documents `FunctionSurfaceMatch::Certain` as including `defmodule`/`defprotocol`/`defimpl` heads.

The implementation excludes those forms:

- A matching `ScopeForm::Function` returns `Certain` at `:2301-2304`.
- A `ScopeForm::CompilerService` whose source defines the requested function returns `Certain` at `:2307-2309`.
- A reserved item-macro call returns `Certain` only when `reserved_source_definition` yields a matching `ReservedSourceDefinition::Function`, at `:2365-2369`.
- `ScopeForm::Module`, `ScopeForm::Protocol`, and `ScopeForm::ProtocolImpl` return `None` at `:2318-2321`.
- Reserved module/protocol/impl definitions also return `None` through `Ok(Some(_))` at `:2374`.

This behavior is correct. Module, protocol, and protocol-implementation forms publish or register module-owned state; they do not themselves publish a wanted global function.

The adjacent `item_macro_call_match` documentation at `:2353-2357` should also state explicitly that reserved non-function heads are definitive non-matches, rather than implying every reserved-head match can be `Certain`.

## Work

Correct the two nearby doc comments so they describe the implemented classification exactly. Do not change matching behavior.

## Acceptance

- The `Certain` variant documents only a matching function form, a matching compiler-service function source, and a reserved item-macro call whose decoded definition is a matching function.
- The `item_macro_call_match` comment explicitly says reserved module/protocol/impl heads are definitive `None` results.
- No documentation implies that `defmodule`, `defprotocol`, or `defimpl` publishes a global function.
- The production diff is comment-only.
- Formatting, library tests, and strict clippy pass.
title: FunctionSurfaceMatch docs claim module/protocol heads can be Certain, but those forms cannot publish a global function
